idea.title: Cross-Lingual Transfer and Calibration of Abstention Thresholds in Translated Factual Question Answering
idea.research_problem: Evaluating whether an abstention threshold calibrated on English factual question answering remains reliable when applied to translated Urdu questions, and whether a small separate Urdu calibration set can close the resulting coverage and accuracy gap.
idea.research_gap: Prior work demonstrates that open-domain QA and multi-granularity answer evaluation rely on uncertainty or confidence tuning predominantly in high-resource languages like English. While benchmarks like IrokoBench reveal performance drops on low-resource and translated tasks, there is a bounded search finding that no existing study measures how translation artifacts distort token-probability-based abstention thresholds or whether low-resource calibration sets can recover optimal coverage-risk trade-offs.
idea.methodology: We freeze an open-access model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct via HuggingFace) and evaluate its generation probabilities on English factual QA datasets (e.g., EntityQuestions) and their machine-translated Urdu counterparts from IrokoBench. We compute softmax-based predictive entropy and max-probability scores over output token distributions. We establish an English-calibrated abstention threshold to target a fixed risk level (e.g., 10% error rate). We then construct a separate Urdu calibration subset to fit a shifted threshold via temperature scaling and quantile adjustment, measuring the resulting impact on selective prediction accuracy and coverage.
idea.expected_contribution: We hypothesize that English-calibrated abstention thresholds suffer from severe over-confidence or under-confidence when transferred zero-shot to translated Urdu questions due to tokenization and perplexity shifts. We further hypothesize that a minor domain-matched Urdu calibration set will realign the risk-coverage curve without requiring model parameter updates.
idea.experimental_setup: We use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct via local HuggingFace transformers. The evaluation dataset comprises 1,000 English question-answer pairs and their professional or machine-translated Urdu equivalents from IrokoBench. We split the Urdu data into a calibration set (300 samples) and a test set (700 samples). We compare zero-shot transfer of the English threshold against the Urdu-calibrated threshold using selective accuracy and risk-coverage area under the curve (RC-AUC).
idea.evaluation_strategy: We report selective classification performance via Risk-Coverage curves. The calibration split determines the decision threshold for a target error rate of 0.10. The test split measures actual empirical risk and coverage. Confidence aggregation relies on sequence-level probability normalization. Statistical significance is tested using paired permutation tests across bootstrap resamples.
feasibility_assumptions: Token-level output probabilities can be fully extracted from the open-weight Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model via local inference.
Machine-translated Urdu evaluation data from IrokoBench accurately represents low-resource factual QA structural patterns.
A calibration subset of 300 instances is sufficient to estimate reliable quantile thresholds without severe overfitting.

assumption_checks.assumption: The open-weight model provides direct, unconstrained access to complete target-token logits for probability extraction.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Run a forward pass on 50 pilot examples and verify extraction of output token log-probabilities.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: 100% success rate in retrieving exact log-probabilities for generated tokens.
assumption_checks.fallback: Switch to score-based verbalized confidence extraction if logit access fails.

assumption_checks.assumption: The 300-sample Urdu calibration set provides stable quantile estimates for the abstention threshold.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Compute bootstrap variance of the estimated threshold across 50 resamplings of the calibration set.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Standard deviation of the threshold is below 5% of the mean threshold value.
assumption_checks.fallback: Apply Laplace smoothing and defensive quantile interpolation to stabilize estimates.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Utilizes model uncertainty and response decoding strategies for open-domain factual question answering.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Focuses exclusively on multi-granularity English evaluation rather than cross-lingual transfer of abstention thresholds to low-resource translated data.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Confirm whether multi-granularity scoring interacts with cross-lingual probability shifts in Urdu.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Evaluates open and proprietary large language models on African and low-resource multilingual benchmarks including translate-test settings.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Assesses static benchmark accuracy rather than dynamic abstention threshold calibration and selective prediction risk-coverage trade-offs.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Test whether translate-test approaches alter uncertainty calibration compared to native-language prompting.

idea.core_hypothesis: Abstention thresholds optimized on English factual QA fail to maintain target error rates when applied zero-shot to translated Urdu questions, but a small separate Urdu calibration set restores optimal risk-coverage performance.
idea.distinctive_mechanism: Empirically isolating and correcting the cross-lingual threshold shift in token-probability-based selective prediction using a minimal target-language calibration split.
idea.minimum_test: Evaluate Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 100 English and 100 translated Urdu QA pairs, applying an English-derived confidence threshold versus an Urdu-calibrated threshold, and measure coverage at a fixed 10% error rate.
